examples.ko: 누가 뒤따라오는 것 같아서 돌아보니 제 그림자였어요.
examples.en: I felt someone following me, but when I looked back, it was my shadow.
The puppy keeps following me.

examples.ko: 먼저 가 계세요. 제가 곧 뒤따라올게요.
examples.en: Please go ahead. I'll come along right after you.
The children followed the teacher in a line.

examples.ko: 택시가 우리 차를 계속 뒤따라와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled because a taxi kept following our car.
My friend came along ten minutes later.

explain: 말하는 사람이 있는 쪽으로 누군가 뒤에서 따라올 때 써요. 멀어지는 쪽이면 '뒤따라가다'를 써요. '약속 장소에 먼저 가 있을게요, 뒤따라오세요'처럼 나중에 오라고 말할 때도 좋아요.

phrases.en: Please follow me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에서 안내하며 따라오라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when leading and telling someone to follow.

phrases.en: Please go in first. I'll follow you in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 그쪽으로 오겠다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you will come to that place later.

phrases.en: The child follows the mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤따라오다'보다 짧고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shorter than 뒤따라오다 and more common.

explain_en: Spoken — someone follows behind and arrives where you are (강아지) Use it when someone follows behind toward where the speaker is. If they move away from the speaker, use '뒤따라가다'. It is also handy for telling someone to come later, as in 'I'll be at the meeting spot, please follow after me'.

en: to step aside; to move aside; to stand aside

examples.en: When the ambulance came, the cars moved aside.

examples.ko: 좁은 계단에서는 서로 한쪽으로 비켜서면 돼요.
examples.en: On a narrow staircase, you can both step to one side.
I stepped aside for a moment and then walked on.

examples.ko: 문 옆에 비켜서서 사람들이 내리기를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I stood aside by the door and waited for people to get off.
I stepped to one side, but I still bumped into someone.

examples.ko: 엘리베이터 앞에서 길을 막지 말고 비켜서야 해요.
examples.en: In front of the elevator, don't block the way; you should step aside.

explain: '비키다'는 길에서 몸이나 물건을 옮겨 자리를 내줄 때 쓰고, '비켜서다'는 비켜서 어느 쪽에 서 있는 모습까지 담아요. 부탁할 때는 '좀 비켜 주세요'라고 해요. '비켜!'는 반말이라 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: When a bike comes, I move to the side.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리를 내주려고 몸이나 물건을 옮기는 동작을 말하고, 서 있는 모습은 담지 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means moving out of the way, without the sense of then standing there.
phrases.en_equiv: to move out of the way

phrases.en: People stepped aside to one side of the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 쪽으로 비켜서는지 말할 때 '한쪽으로', '옆으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 한쪽으로 or 옆으로 to say which way someone steps aside.
phrases.en_equiv: to step aside to one side

phrases.en: Excuse me, could you please move aside?
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 비켜 달라고 정중하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to ask someone to let you pass.

explain_en: Stand up and give way, used when asking others (비켜서 주세요) '비키다' means to move out of the way (a body or an object), while '비켜서다' also suggests standing off to one side. When asking, say '좀 비켜 주세요'. '비켜!' is casual speech and can sound rude.

t90.ax: When the ambulance came, the cars moved aside.

en: to transport; to convey; to carry

examples.en: A truck carries the goods to the warehouse.
Workers carried the moving boxes to the new house.
The two of us will carry the heavy box.
A vehicle carrying a patient to the hospital passed by.
After moving the goods, I took a rest.
Please leave the carried luggage in front of the door.

explain: 무거운 짐이나 물건을 트럭·배·기계 등으로 한 곳에서 다른 곳으로 옮길 때 써요. '옮기다'보다 딱딱하고 일하는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '운반'은 '운반 비용'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: Heavy furniture has a high transport cost.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '운반'에 '비용'이 붙은 짝말로, 물건을 옮기는 데 드는 돈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun pair meaning the money needed to move goods.

phrases.en: Please carry this box up to the second floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일하는 사람에게 정중하게 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request, usually to someone doing the work.

phrases.en: My friend and I moved the desk into the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운반하다'보다 부드럽고 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 같은 뜻의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more everyday word with a similar meaning.

explain_en: Physically moving things, by hand or vehicle, any scale. Use it for moving heavy goods from one place to another by truck, ship, or machine. It is stiffer than '옮기다' and feels like work. The noun 운반 appears in '운반 비용' (transport cost).

t90.ax: After moving the goods, I took a rest.

examples.en: Bedtime is eleven at night.
Don't look at your smartphone before bed.
In the dormitory, lights-out is at twelve.
I drink warm tea before going to bed.

examples.ko: 취침 후에는 방의 불을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: After bedtime, please turn off the room light.
You get healthier if you go to bed regularly too.

explain: 잠자리에 드는 일을 격식 있게 나타내는 한자어예요. 일상 대화에서는 '자다', '잠자리에 들다'를 쓰고, 기숙사나 군대의 규칙, 안내문에서 '취침 시간'처럼 써요. 반대는 '기상'이에요.

phrases.en: The students go to bed at ten.
phrases.nuance_ko: '취침'에 '하다'를 붙인 동사예요. 기숙사나 군대 같은 곳에서 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 취침, used in formal settings like dormitories or the military.

phrases.example: 우리 기숙사는 취침 시간이 열한 시예요.
phrases.en: Bedtime in our dormitory is eleven o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자야 하는 시간이에요. 규칙이나 안내문에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The time you must go to bed; common in rules and notices.

phrases.en: I was tired yesterday, so I went to bed early.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취침과 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 취침, but a natural everyday expression.

explain_en: It is a formal Sino-Korean word for going to bed. In daily conversation use '자다' or '잠자리에 들다'; '취침 시간' (bedtime) appears in rules and notices at dormitories and the military. The opposite is '기상' (getting up).

examples.ko: 빨간불에 길을 건너면 안 돼요. 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: You must not cross the street on a red light. It's the law.
The traffic light turned red, so the car stopped.
When the red light comes on, wait a moment.
The light was red and someone was crossing, so I was startled.
The red light at this crosswalk is too long.
Bicycles also have to stop at a red light.

explain: 반의어는 '파란불'이에요. 신호등의 초록색 불도 한국어에서는 보통 '파란불'이라고 말해요. 정확히 말할 때는 '초록불'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I overworked, and my health started showing warning signs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신호등이 아니라 몸이나 사업, 상황에 '위험하다'는 신호가 나타났다는 뜻이에요. '건강에 빨간불이 켜졌다'가 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is not about a traffic light but means a danger signal has appeared for your body, business or situation. '건강에 빨간불이 켜졌다' is the most common use.
phrases.en_equiv: a red flag; warning signs appear

explain_en: Literal red light, everyday and spoken. The opposite is '파란불'. Even the green traffic light is usually called '파란불' in Korean, though '초록불' is also used when being precise.

t90.ax: Bicycles also have to stop at a red light.

examples.en: The last uphill stretch was really hard.

examples.ko: 자전거로 오르막을 올라갈 때는 기어를 바꿔요.
examples.en: When I go uphill by bike, I change gears.

examples.ko: 우리 집 앞은 오르막이라서 겨울에 미끄러워요.
examples.en: The road in front of my house is a slope, so it's slippery in winter.
When it snows, walk slowly on uphill roads.
After the uphill comes a downhill.
I was out of breath on the uphill, so I rested for a moment.

explain: 반대말은 '내리막'이에요. '오르막길'이라고 길 이름처럼 붙여 쓰는 경우도 많아요. 사람의 인생이 좋아졌다 나빠졌다 하는 것도 '오르막 내리막'에 비유해서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I get out of breath on the uphill road.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르막'보다 길이라는 점이 분명해서 길 이야기에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes it clear it's a road, so it is more common in talk about paths.

phrases.en: I climbed the slope slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라가는 동작을 말할 때 '오르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '오르다' to describe the act of climbing.

phrases.en: Uphill stretches are hard when riding a bike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 올라가는 길이 힘들다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that going uphill is tiring.

explain_en: The opposite is '내리막' (downhill). It's also common to say '오르막길' (uphill road). People also compare the ups and downs of life to '오르막 내리막'.

examples.en: A young child should not sit in the front passenger seat.
I will open the passenger door for you.
The passenger seat is empty, so please sit there.

examples.ko: 조수석에서 지도를 보며 길을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: From the passenger seat, I looked at the map and gave directions.

examples.ko: 새 차의 조수석은 의자가 정말 편해요.
examples.en: The passenger seat in the new car is really comfortable.
The window on the passenger side will not close.

explain: 운전하는 자리는 '운전석', 그 옆자리는 '조수석', 뒤쪽은 '뒷자리'라고 해요. 택시에서 손님이 앞자리에 앉을 때도 '조수석'이라고 말하는 사람이 있어요.

phrases.en: I rode in the front passenger seat of Dad's car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전하는 사람 옆자리에 탈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when riding in the seat next to the driver.
phrases.en_equiv: to ride in the passenger seat

phrases.en: You must also wear the seat belt in the passenger seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자동차 안전을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears when talking about car safety.

phrases.en: I put my bag on the passenger seat next to the driver's seat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '운전석'과 같이 써서 위치를 분명하게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '운전석' to make the position clear.

explain_en: Seat beside the driver in a car. The driver's seat is '운전석', the seat beside it is '조수석', and the back is '뒷자리'. Some people also say '조수석' when a customer sits in the front seat of a taxi.

en: to get off; to alight; to disembark

examples.en: I get off at the next stop.
After getting off the subway, I got lost.
To get off the bus, you have to press the bell.

examples.ko: 하차하는 승객이 다 내린 뒤에 타세요.
examples.en: Please board after the passengers getting off have all left.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 건강 문제로 드라마에서 하차했어요.
examples.en: That actor left the drama because of health problems.
My friend got off at the station and took a taxi.

explain: 하차하다는 안내 방송이나 공지에서 자주 들리는 말이고, 평소에 말할 때는 보통 '내리다'를 써요. 반대말은 '승차하다'예요. 방송 프로그램에서 빠지는 것도 '하차'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I get off at the next station.
phrases.nuance_ko: 평소에 말할 때는 '하차하다'보다 '내리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech, '내리다' is used instead of '하차하다'.

phrases.example: 내릴 곳이 가까우면 하차 벨을 눌러요.
phrases.en: Press the stop bell when your stop is near.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스에서 내리겠다고 알리는 벨을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The bell on a bus that signals you want to get off.

phrases.en: I'll call you after I get off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내린 다음에 할 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for what happens after getting off.

explain_en: Formal Sino-Korean; announcements, signs, official notices. 하차하다 is often heard in announcements and notices; in daily speech people usually say '내리다'. The opposite is '승차하다'. Leaving a TV program is also called '하차'.

t90.ax: I get off at the next stop.

examples.en: A helicopter flew over the mountain.
They moved the injured person to the hospital by helicopter.

examples.ko: 헬기 소리가 너무 커서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The helicopter noise was so loud that I couldn't sleep.
A fire helicopter is putting out the wildfire.

examples.ko: 아이는 헬기를 타 보고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: The child wants to ride in a helicopter.

examples.ko: 뉴스 헬기에서 도로 상황을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The news helicopter showed the road conditions.

explain: 헬기는 '헬리콥터'를 줄인 말이에요. 말할 때와 뉴스에서 모두 자주 써요. 구조, 산불 진화, 군용에 쓰는 헬기 이야기가 많이 나와요.

phrases.example: 아이가 하늘의 헬리콥터를 보고 손을 흔들었어요.
phrases.en: The child saw a helicopter in the sky and waved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헬기의 원래 말이고, 조금 더 길고 또렷하게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 헬기, sounding a little longer and clearer.

phrases.example: 산불 때문에 헬기가 여러 대 떴어요.
phrases.en: Several helicopters took off because of the wildfire.
phrases.nuance_ko: 헬기가 공중으로 올라갈 때 '뜨다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 뜨다 when a helicopter lifts into the air.

phrases.example: 구조 헬기가 바다 위를 날고 있어요.
phrases.en: A rescue helicopter is flying over the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 구하는 일을 하는 헬기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A helicopter used to rescue people.

explain_en: Short form of the loanword; common in news and quick speech. 헬기 is the shortened form of '헬리콥터'. It is common in both speech and the news. It often comes up in stories about rescue, firefighting, and the military.

t90.ax: A helicopter flew over the mountain.

examples.en: Our school starts the new semester on March 2.
The vacation ended and school started again today.

examples.ko: 내일 개학하면 친구들을 다시 만날 수 있어요.
examples.en: When school starts tomorrow, I can see my friends again.

examples.ko: 아이들이 개학할 때까지 가족 여행을 다녀올 거예요.
examples.en: We will go on a family trip before the kids go back to school.

examples.ko: 개학하는 날 아침에는 늘 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: On the morning school starts, I always feel heavy-hearted.
School has started, so the streets are crowded again.

explain: 방학이 끝나고 새 학기가 시작될 때 써요. 반대는 '방학하다'예요. 보통 '학교가 개학하다'처럼 학교를 주어로 써요. '입학하다'는 학교에 처음 들어갈 때 쓰니까 달라요.

phrases.en: I finished all my homework before school started.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개학하다'에 '-기 전에'를 붙여 개학 전의 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-기 전에' to 개학하다 lets you talk about things you do before school starts.

phrases.example: 개학하면 친구들을 다시 만날 수 있어요.
phrases.en: When school starts, I can meet my friends again.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)면'을 붙여 개학한 뒤에 할 일이나 생길 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-(으)면' lets you talk about what will happen once school starts.

phrases.en: On the first day of school, I overslept and was late.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 대신 명사 '개학'을 써서 개학한 날을 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This uses the noun 개학 to refer to the day school starts.

explain_en: School only: a new semester begins. Use it when vacation ends and a new term starts. The opposite is '방학하다'. It is usually said with the school as the subject, like '학교가 개학하다'. '입학하다' is for entering a school for the first time, so it is different.

en: to be afraid; to be scared

examples.ko: 우리 강아지가 큰 천둥소리에 겁먹고 침대 밑에 숨었어요.
examples.en: Our puppy got scared by the loud thunder and hid under the bed.
Don't be scared, it doesn't hurt at all.

examples.ko: 처음 비행기를 탔을 때 많이 겁먹었어요.
examples.en: I was really scared the first time I rode an airplane.

examples.ko: 뭘 그렇게 겁먹어요? 아무 일도 아니에요.
examples.en: What are you so scared of? It's nothing.
He looked at the teacher with a frightened face.

examples.ko: 겁먹을 필요 없어요. 면접은 금방 끝나요.
examples.en: There's no need to be scared. The interview ends quickly.

explain: '무서워하다'와 비슷하지만 '겁먹다'는 두려움이 마음에 들어와 움츠러든 모습을 말해요. '겁먹지 마'처럼 격려하는 말로 자주 나와요. '겁이 나다'는 두려운 마음이 저절로 생기는 느낌이고, '겁을 먹다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요.

phrases.en: The child looked at Mom with a scared face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '겁먹다'가 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 모양으로, 무서워하는 표정을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of 겁먹다, used to describe a frightened expression.

phrases.en: Don't be scared, I'll be right next to you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대방을 안심시키며 격려할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서는 '겁먹지 마'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite, encouraging way to reassure someone; with close friends you say '겁먹지 마'.

phrases.en: I was startled by the loud noise and got scared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 무서워진 상태를 과거로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, saying that someone already became scared.

explain_en: It is similar to '무서워하다', but '겁먹다' shows someone shrinking back because fear has taken hold. It often appears in encouraging phrases like '겁먹지 마'. '겁이 나다' means fear arises on its own, and you can also split this word as '겁을 먹다'.

examples.en: The ball rolled slowly toward the goal.
The goalkeeper defended the goal until the end.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 골문 앞에서 기회를 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: That player missed a chance right in front of the goal.
Before the match I checked whether the goal wobbled.

examples.ko: 상대 골문까지 달리는 데 오 초 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took five seconds to run to the opponent's goal.
A net hangs on the goal.

explain: '골대'는 기둥과 가로대로 된 틀을 가리킬 때가 많고, '골문'은 공이 들어가는 입구 쪽을 가리켜요. 축구, 하키 같은 경기에서 써요.

phrases.en: The players are gathered in front of the goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 골문 가까운 곳을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the area near the goal.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 골문을 지키는 일을 해요.
phrases.en: That player guards the goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 골키퍼가 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe what a goalkeeper does.

phrases.en: The ball went into the goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공이 골로 들어갔다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the ball goes into the goal.

explain_en: The physical goal in soccer or hockey that a ball enters. 골대 often points to the frame made of posts and a crossbar, while 골문 points to the opening the ball goes into. Both are used in sports like soccer and hockey.

examples.ko: 큰길 위에 새 영화 광고판이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: A billboard for a new movie was put up over the main road.

examples.ko: 버스 정류장 광고판을 보고 가수 이름을 알았어요.
examples.en: I learned the singer's name from the ad board at the bus stop.

examples.ko: 광고판에는 신제품 사진이 크게 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The billboard shows a big picture of the new product.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 광고판의 불빛이 흐리게 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the light of the billboard looks blurry.
I decided to meet my friend in front of the billboard.
I heard the old billboard will be replaced with a new one tomorrow.

explain: '간판'은 가게가 자기 이름을 걸어 두는 판이고, 광고판은 광고를 보여 주는 판이에요. 불빛이 나오는 화면으로 된 것은 '전광판'이라고 해요. 길가나 건물 위에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: We hung a new billboard in front of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고판을 달아 놓는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for putting up a billboard.

phrases.en: My friend appeared on a billboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 광고판에 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when a person or product appears on a billboard.

phrases.en: I'm waiting for my friend in front of the billboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속 장소를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to name a meeting spot.

explain_en: Physical board displaying ads, outdoors. A '간판' is the sign a shop hangs with its own name, while 광고판 shows advertisements. One made of a lit-up screen is called a '전광판'. You can see them by the road or on top of buildings.
